title: Enterprise Support: Outage claim credits
content:
Enterprise Support — Outage claim credits.

## Policy clauses

For an outage service credit financial posting, an approved review has decision eligible and positive approved credit amount for the exact source charge; this gate does not constrain filing or reviewing the request.

For an outage service credit request being filed, the outage claim is filed no later than credit claim days after the official incident closes.

For a newly filed claim, current handling time is its recorded notice time; the request is recorded immediately.

Later review and credit use that recorded notice time to evaluate the same boundary, so a timely request does not expire while awaiting review.

Add credit claim days UTC calendar dates to official incident closure time, preserving its time of day; calendar dates are counted without substituting business days or elapsed-hour periods.

Equality at the deadline qualifies; a later claim is rejected without a credit.

The provider incident must be completed, with cause outside outage exclusions.

Availability at or above availability target percentage gives no credit.

Below the target choose the first descending availability credit bands entry whose minimum is no greater than the recorded availability percentage.

Multiply the original source charge pretax net amount by that fraction; subtract the net service-credit component of prior credits for that exact source, and cap total service credits at credit cap fraction of that original net amount.

Floor the additional credit at zero and round with monetary decimal precision and rounding convention.

Apply the original tax component proportionately.

A review writes its nonnegative approved result; a financial credit writes the negative approved amount only after that approved review exists.

This service-credit branch applies only to source subtype outage service credit; invoice correction accounting applies only to source subtype correction.

Excluded incidents, ineligible reviews and zero remaining entitlement result in no financial write.

A request for consequential-loss compensation is not covered.

A service-credit financial posting requires an approved review with decision eligible and positive approved credit amount; the request and incident alone cannot authorize the financial posting.

## Authoritative evidence

For an outage service credit request being filed, the outage claim is filed no later than credit claim days after the official incident closes. The authoritative system record must establish the condition before the action. Its evidence comprises support event reference, official incident closure time, recorded notice time. Correlate the action to the same support event reference.

For an outage service credit financial posting, an approved review has decision eligible and positive approved credit amount for the exact source charge; this gate does not constrain filing or reviewing the request. The authoritative system record must establish the condition before the action. Its evidence comprises support event reference, original source reference, status, decision, approved credit amount. Correlate the action to the same original source reference.

## Hypothetical case

A hypothetical claim filed exactly at the official incident closure time advanced by the prescribed claim calendar dates satisfies the filing deadline. A claim filed one second later misses it. A later review uses the timely recorded notice time, so review delay does not make that claim late.
